currentContext.business: The Company manufactures industrial yarn and tyre cord fabric, and has the capability to supply treated (dipped) fabric - a ready-to-use product widely preferred by tyre manufacturers - a capability further strengthened by an upgradation of its dipping facility. During the year it expanded its scope from the production of industrial yarn to engineering capabilities, partnering for the supply of fuel cubes to the Europe and USA markets and entering a contract manufacturing agreement for hydro-optic disinfectant UV water treatment solutions for an Israel based customer. Its MD&A discusses the Indian defence sector as the sector whose liberalised industrial atmosphere the Company is engaged in taking advantage of; its Rayon Undertaking was demerged into the Company from DCM Shriram Industries Limited under an NCLT-approved Composite Scheme of Arrangement.

currentContext.strengths: High-value-added product mix: during the year the share of treated (dipped) fabric in total exports to tyre Companies was more than 80%, described as reflecting a strong base of high-value-added products|Capability to supply treated fabric, a ready-to-use product widely preferred by tyre manufacturers, further strengthened through upgradation of the dipping facility|Captive energy base - a 2.11 MW solar plant commissioned earlier plus a progressive shift from fossil fuels to agrofuels (mustard husk, now pelletised) - reducing grid reliance and operating cost|Natural FX hedge from annual fixation of export product prices and imported pulp costs, which mitigates foreign exchange risk to a large extent|Broadening from a single-product industrial yarn base into engineering and contract manufacturing (fuel cubes, UV water treatment) for overseas customers
currentContext.strategies: Move up the value chain in tyre cord fabric - supplying treated (dipped), ready-to-use fabric preferred by tyre manufacturers, with the dipping facility upgraded to improve product quality and operational efficiency|Expand scope from production of industrial yarn into engineering capabilities - supply of fuel cubes to the Europe and USA markets and contract manufacturing of hydro-optic disinfectant UV water treatment solutions for an Israel based customer|Reduce energy dependence and operating cost through captive generation: a new 40 TPH boiler, a husk pellet machine converting loose mustard husk into pellets, and an earlier-commissioned 2.11 MW solar plant, with a progressive shift from fossil fuels to agrofuels|Optimise cost structures through alternative sourcing, engage closely with global customers and maintain operational efficiencies so as to benefit from a gradual recovery in end-market demand|Pursue R&D in new energy by giving a Hydrogen Gas Project for R&D to a Research Centre|Strengthen internal control and systems - digital tracking of sensitive inventory with real-time monitoring and cross-unit integration, stronger forecasting and accountability, and SAP RISE implementation to improve data flow and accuracy|Participate in the liberalised Indian defence industrial environment, which the MD&A identifies as the sector the Company is engaged in taking advantage of
currentContext.expansion: The Company's disclosed expansion is concentrated in energy, fuel handling and product upgradation rather than in nameplate capacity addition. It is installing a new 40 TPH boiler which will enhance fuel efficiency, increase captive power generation and reduce reliance on grid supply, thereby mitigating the risk of supply interruptions. It has installed a husk pellet machine to convert loose mustard husk into pellets - removing dust and stones during processing, allowing bunker storage, reducing open storage, enabling continuous conveyor-based fuel feeding, lowering manpower requirements and cutting suspended particulate emissions. A 2.11 MW solar power plant commissioned earlier continues to operate, supplementing captive and grid power. A Hydrogen Gas Project has been given for R&D to a Research Centre. On the product side, the dipping facility has been upgraded, strengthening the capability to supply treated (dipped) fabric and improving product quality and operational efficiency. The Company has also expanded its scope from industrial yarn into engineering capabilities, partnering for fuel cube supply to Europe and USA and entering a contract manufacturing agreement for hydro-optic disinfectant UV water treatment solutions for an Israel based customer. No commissioning dates or project costs are stated in the routed narrative.
currentContext.mdna: Near-term demand is expected to remain measured; the Company is proactively managing macroeconomic and sectoral challenges and is positioned to benefit from a gradual recovery in end-market demand as conditions stabilise|Sales volume declined during the year due to lower demand and the geopolitical situation in the Middle East, reducing profitability - turnover at Rs. 451.17 crore versus Rs. 573.68 crore, lower by 21.36% due to the international market scenario|Overall profitability is expected to improve as the energy and efficiency initiatives (40 TPH boiler, husk pellet machine, solar plant) progress|Product mix is a margin lever: more than 80% of exports to tyre companies were treated (dipped) fabric, described as a strong base of high-value-added products|Input costs: sulphur and sulphuric acid prices rose significantly on the Middle East situation with further increases expected; caustic soda and charcoal rose marginally and are expected to remain at similar levels; husk prices were higher though some softening is expected in the current year|Logistics and insurance costs had increased on macroeconomic and geopolitical factors and are being monitored closely|Currency: the Rupee depreciated 4.98% against the US Dollar in H2 2025 (peaking at 6.46% in December), but annual fixation of export product prices and imported pulp costs provides a natural hedge|Macro backdrop: forecasts have moderated India's GDP growth outlook for FY27 to approximately 6.4% on rising crude oil prices and a slight softening in domestic consumption|Defence sector opportunity: rising government expenditure and 'Make in India', Positive Indigenisation Lists, 74% FDI via the automatic route, Defence Industrial Corridors in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, and modernisation plans providing a steady pipeline of opportunities

risks.risk: Foreign-exchange exposure on exports and imported pulp
risks.note: The Rupee depreciated significantly by 4.98% against the US Dollar during H2 2025, peaking at 6.46% in December; the Board's report states currency volatility poses a risk, mitigated to a large extent by annual fixation of export product prices and imported pulp costs (Directors' Report).

risks.risk: Import dependence for pulp, the key raw material
risks.note: The Company's cost base includes imported pulp whose cost is fixed annually, so sourcing and landed-cost movements sit outside its control (Directors' Report).

risks.risk: Measured near-term end-market demand and macroeconomic/sectoral headwinds
risks.note: The Board states near-term demand is expected to remain measured and that the Company is proactively managing macroeconomic and sectoral challenges, with recovery dependent on external conditions stabilising (Directors' Report).

risks.risk: Complexity and estimation judgement in the Rayon Undertaking demerger
risks.note: The auditor designated the NCLT-approved demerger of the Rayon Undertaking from DCM Shriram Industries Limited (order dated 21 November 2025, appointed date 1 April 2023, accounted as a common control combination under Ind AS 103 Appendix C) a Key Audit Matter, citing its magnitude and the significant estimate and judgement in identifying and allocating assets, liabilities and related equity balances transferred (Independent Auditor's Report).

risks.risk: Loss-making year - the audited outcome for FY26 was a loss
risks.note: The auditor's opinion refers to the state of affairs as at 31 March 2026 and to the Company's loss and other comprehensive loss for the year, i.e. the year closed in a loss position (Independent Auditor's Report).
